governing_table.code: Georgia State Minimum Standard Plumbing Code (International Plumbing Code with Georgia State Amendments)
governing_table.edition: 2024 International Plumbing Code, Georgia amendments revised January 1, 2026
governing_table.table: Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures (the building code's Table 2902.1 is the same table; Georgia makes the same two deletions in Section 2902)
governing_table.quote: The INTERNATIONAL PLUMBING CODE, 2024 Edition, published by the International Code Council, when used in conjunction with these and any other Georgia State Amendments to the INTERNATIONAL PLUMBING CODE, 2024 EDITION, shall constitute the official Georgia State Minimum Standard Plumbing Code.
governing_table.note: Georgia's amendments to Table 403.1 delete the service sink column and add text to the residential row only: 'The remainder of the table remains unchanged.' The table rows themselves were read on UpCodes' copy of the Georgia Plumbing Code 2024 (https://up.codes/viewer/georgia/ipc-2024/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings), a secondary source.

cities_may_amend_note.text: A city or county may adopt local amendments that are not less stringent than the state code, based on local climatic, geologic, topographic or public safety factors, after sending them to DCA for review. DCA recommends only.
cities_may_amend_note.quote: The requirements in the proposed local amendment cannot be less stringent than the requirements in the state minimum standard code.

office.row_label: No. 2, Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, nonmedical professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.row_label: No. 1, Assembly: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200 [lavatories]

sex_split.text: Half the occupants are counted as each sex, unless approved statistical data show another split. Georgia deleted the model code's second exception, which lets an all-gender multi-user room be counted on the whole occupant load.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex. | Georgia amendment: *Delete 403.1.1 'Fixture calculations' Exception 2 without substitution. (Effective January 1, 2026)

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number, per sex. With several occupancies in one building, add the fractions first, then round up.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets in assembly (restaurants) and educational occupancies, and up to 50% elsewhere (offices). Georgia did not amend this section. Each urinal used by the public or employees needs a partition or wall on each side.
urinal_substitution.quote: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in all other occupancies.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate rooms for each sex are not required where the space holds 15 or fewer people in total, in a business occupancy of 25 or fewer, or in a mercantile occupancy of 100 or fewer. Rooms made up of single-user toilet rooms need not be designated by sex. Georgia deleted the model code's sixth exception (shared all-gender rooms).
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. | Georgia amendment: *Delete 403.2 'Separate facilities' Exception 6 without substitution. (Effective January 1, 2026)

occupant_load.text: The plumbing code takes the number of occupants from the building code. Table 1004.5 of the building code: business areas 150 square feet gross per person; assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; educational classroom area 20 net. Georgia's Codes Reference Guide makes the Life Safety Code (NFPA 101) the primary code for means of egress, so a local official may use its occupant load table instead; that table was not read.
occupant_load.quote: The number of occupants shall be determined by the International Building Code. | Business areas | 150 gross ; Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net ; Classroom area | 20 net

worked_examples.how: 25 women and 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 1 = 0.5, so none.
50 women and 50 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 50/25 = 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 2 = 1.
100 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1, total 3 each. Urinals up to 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3, total 5 each. Urinals up to 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 1 per 75: 25/75 = 0.33, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/75 = 0.67, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1, so none.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2 each. Urinals up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3 each. Urinals up to 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 each. 1 per 50: 25/50 = 0.5, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1, so none.
50 each. 50/50 = 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1, so none.
100 each. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals up to 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2.

fixtures.confidence_note: Georgia's amendments were read on DCA's own PDF (official). The unamended rows and Sections 403.1.1, 403.2 and 424.2 were read on UpCodes' Georgia copy, because codes.iccsafe.org serves the text by script only.

hdpe_fire.section: 2024 International Building Code Section 803.9, not amended by Georgia; Section 202 definition of Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | Definition: Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish. The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings [...]
hdpe_fire.caveat: Georgia's amendment packet does not touch Chapter 8, so 803.9 stands in the state building code. But the packet's Codes Reference Guide lists 'Interior Finish | LSC | NONE' (primary code: Life Safety Code, NFPA 101; supplement: none), and the Safety Fire Commissioner's Rule 120-3-3 says 'Interior finish and trim in proposed (new) buildings shall be regulated by NFPA 101, Life Safety Code'. The Life Safety Code's own HDPE text could not be read (NFPA's free viewer needs a sign-in), so which text a Georgia plan reviewer applies to partitions is not confirmed.

access.state_standard: Georgia Accessibility Code, Rules of the Safety Fire Commissioner Chapter 120-3-20 (effective January 1, 2015): adopts the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design as the state minimum. The state building code's Chapter 11 is deleted, so ICC A117.1 does not come in through the building code for commercial restrooms (the rule uses ICC/ANSI A117.1-2003 only for apartments).

differences_note.text: No stall differences found. Rule 120-3-20 contains no modification to sections 213, 603, 604 or 609 of the 2010 ADA Standards; its Georgia-specific items concern parking counts, assembly seating, apartments and the definition of renovation.
differences_note.quote: Unless otherwise stated in this chapter, the minimum adopted standards for accessibility in the State shall be the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design for Titles II and III Facilities, published in the Federal Register, September 15, 2010, and taking effect on March 15, 2012.
differences_note.also: Georgia IBC amendment: '*Delete Chapter 11 'Accessibility' entirely without substitution. {Cross-reference in State law: Title 30, Chapter 3 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A) and the Rules and Regulations of the Georgia Safety Fire Commissioner.}' (https://dca.georgia.gov/document/document/ibc-2026-amendment-packet-2024-edition/download)

renovation_note.text: The rule's definition of renovation covers replaced components: a replaced component must meet the standard, repairs excepted.
renovation_note.quote: Any component of a building, structure, or facility, which is replaced, except for the purpose of repair, or moved, shall be required to meet the ANSI A117.1 Standard as specified in this Code section, including an accessible route as defined in the ANSI A117.1 Standard

access.process: No state registration or separate accessibility plan-review filing was found in Rule 120-3-20. The Safety Fire Commissioner (State Fire Marshal) enforces the code in buildings under his jurisdiction; the Board of Regents and the local governing authority enforce it in the others. An owner can request an exemption from a specific requirement with a sworn written statement; the decision is recorded within 45 days. The State ADA Coordinator's Office publishes the code and technical bulletins.
access.process_quote: The Safety Fire Commissioner or, where applicable, the Board of Regents or the local governing authority having jurisdiction over the buildings in question shall be responsible for making a final determination as to whether or not an exemption shall be granted.

single_user.rule: A single-user toilet room, including a family or assisted-use room, must be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex, and its fixtures count toward the required total. Georgia did not amend this section. No Georgia statute on single-user restroom signs was found.
single_user.quote: Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.

all_gender_shared.rule: Georgia deleted the two model-code provisions that let a shared all-gender multi-user room stand in for separate men's and women's rooms. Where toilets are required, the required ones go in separate facilities for each sex, unless a small-occupancy exception applies or single-user rooms are used. The code as adopted does not say whether a shared all-gender room may be added on top of the required separate rooms: ask the local building department. Every toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door, and every urinal a partitioned space, in any multi-user room.
all_gender_shared.quote: *Delete 403.1.1 'Fixture calculations' Exception 2 without substitution. (Effective January 1, 2026) *Delete 403.2 'Separate facilities' Exception 6 without substitution. (Effective January 1, 2026) | Deleted model text (2024 IPC 403.2 Exception 6, read on UpCodes' Colorado copy): 'Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets in accordance with Section 405.3.4 and for urinals in accordance with Section 405.3.5.' | Kept: '403.2 Separate Facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate toilet facilities shall be provided for each sex.'

use_restrictions.rule: Senate Bill 1 of 2025 (the Riley Gaines Act, O.C.G.A. 20-2-315 for schools and a matching section for colleges, signed April 28, 2025) applies to local school systems, public schools and private schools that compete against them, and to colleges for student athletes. Each covered school must provide separate multiple occupancy restrooms or changing areas on the basis of sex, and for interscholastic competitions must designate each such room for exclusive use by males or by females, with a reasonable accommodation such as a single occupancy restroom. No Georgia statute restricting restroom use in other government or private buildings was found.
use_restrictions.quote: Each covered entity shall provide separate multiple occupancy restrooms or changing areas and sleeping quarters on the basis of sex, and such facilities shall be comparable to such facilities provided for students of the other sex. [...] Designate each multiple occupancy restroom or changing area and sleeping quarters for exclusive use by males or for exclusive use by females; and (ii) Provide a reasonable accommodation to individuals who are unwilling or unable to use a multiple occupancy restroom or changing area or sleeping quarters designated for each such individual's sex. [...] 'Covered entity' means local school systems, public schools, and participating private schools.

public_wage.rates_url: https://sam.gov/wage-determinations (federal Davis-Bacon wage determinations, federally funded work only)
public_wage.quote: Twenty-four states do not have prevailing wage laws. These States are Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, [...]
public_wage.note: Read through the fetch tool (dol.gov refused a direct download); the page is the U.S. Department of Labor's table of state prevailing wage thresholds, last revised January 1, 2023. Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded or assisted construction. Whether Atlanta or Savannah sets wage terms in its own contracts is a city-level question.

state_rate_quote.quote: Code 000 - The state sales and use tax rate of 4% is included in all jurisdictions other than 803 Fulton (Cent. Yards) and 805 Fulton (S. Downtn).
state_rate_quote.note: Same chart, effective October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026: 060A Fulton (Atlanta) 8.9; 044A DeKalb (Atlanta) 8.9; 025 Chatham 7. The chart is reissued each quarter.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. A remote seller must collect Georgia state and local tax, at the rate of the delivery location, once it has more than $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 or more separate retail sales of goods delivered into Georgia in the previous or current calendar year. Where tax was not charged at the point of sale, use tax applies on first use in Georgia, at the state and local rate, and the local rate is generally the rate of the county where the buyer receives the goods.
shipped_goods.quote: Thus, effective January 1, 2020, a remote seller that has met one of the thresholds in the previous or current calendar year must collect and remit Georgia sales tax on their taxable sales of tangible personal property delivered to a location in Georgia (including both state tax and local tax, with the local tax rate based on the delivery location). | 'Use tax' is also a term commonly used to refer to the tax imposed on taxable goods and services that were not taxed at the point of sale.

freight_quote.quote: Charges made for delivery, transportation, freight, or shipping and handling are part of the sales price and subject to sales tax in the same manner as the underlying sale. Thus, if a taxable item is sold, and the seller makes a separate charge for delivery, transportation, freight, or shipping and handling, the separate charge is taxable.

install_labor.rule: Not taxed when itemized. Installation charges are left out of the sales price if they are separately stated on the invoice.
install_labor.quote: Itemized charges made for repair labor or installation labor are not subject to sales tax. O.C.G.A. §§ 48-8-2(34)(B)(iv), 48-8-3(23). | [sales price does not include] installation charges if they are separately stated on the invoice, billing, or similar document given to the purchaser

furnish_and_install.rule: A contractor who furnishes and installs materials in improving real property is treated as the consumer of those materials and pays the tax on them when buying or using them. What I read does not say in so many words that the contractor's charge to the owner is untaxed; confirm with the Department.
furnish_and_install.quote: Any person who contracts to furnish tangible personal property and perform services thereunder in constructing, altering, repairing or improving real property in this State is deemed to be the consumer of all tangible personal property used or consumed in performing such contract and shall pay the tax thereon at the time of purchase, use, storage or consumption in this State, whichever occurs first.
furnish_and_install.url: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/georgia/Ga-Comp-R-Regs-R-560-12-2-.26 (rule text, secondary copy; rules.sos.ga.gov returned 403) ; https://dor.georgia.gov/tax-guide-contractors (Department page pointing to the rule)

page.stalls_intro: Georgia's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in the men's room they may take the place of up to half the toilets in an office, and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen on both sides.
page.stalls_after: These are state minimums for the whole building, and a city or county may set stricter ones. An office that holds 25 people or fewer, or any space that holds 15 or fewer, may use one restroom for everyone.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Georgia's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version. In new buildings the State Fire Marshal's rules govern wall finishes, so confirm with your local fire marshal.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Georgia's own access rules adopt the federal standards, and the State Fire Marshal or the local building department enforces them. A stall that is replaced, not just repaired, must meet the current rules.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Georgia and federal stall rules match:** Georgia uses the federal standards for stalls, doors and grab bars as written, so a stall that meets one meets the other.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. Georgia's rules call for separate men's and women's rooms for the toilets a building must have, and the state removed the option that lets a shared all-gender room take their place, so ask your building department before planning one. State law requires public schools, and private schools that compete against them, to provide separate shared restrooms for each sex.
page.public_jobs: Georgia has no state wage law for public construction, so a set wage applies only on federally funded projects, under federal law.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Georgia, installation labor is not taxed when it is listed separately on the invoice. A contractor who supplies and installs the partitions pays the tax on the materials.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable, freight included. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Georgia Department of Revenue
sources: - Georgia building and plumbing codes in force: Georgia Department of Community Affairs, [Current State Minimum Codes for Construction](https://dca.georgia.gov/community-assistance/construction-codes/current-state-minimum-codes-construction), [Georgia State Amendments to the International Plumbing Code (2024 Edition), revised January 1, 2026](https://dca.georgia.gov/document/document/ipc-2026-amendment-packet-2024-edition/download) and [Georgia State Amendments to the International Building Code (2024 Edition), revised January 1, 2026](https://dca.georgia.gov/document/document/ibc-2026-amendment-packet-2024-edition/download). Further amendments take effect January 1, 2027 ([DCA announcement](https://dca.georgia.gov/announcement/2025-12-09/new-codes-jan-2027)); they do not change the toilet counts. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts in Georgia: 2024 International Plumbing Code as adopted by Georgia, Table 403.1 and Sections 403.1.1 (half men, half women; fractions round up), 403.2 (separate rooms and the small-building exceptions), 405.3.4 and 405.3.5 (stalls and urinal screens) and 424.2 (urinals in place of toilets), read on [UpCodes' copy of the Georgia Plumbing Code 2024](https://up.codes/viewer/georgia/ipc-2024/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings), a secondary copy; Georgia's deletions of Exception 2 to 403.1.1 and Exception 6 to 403.2 are in the [state amendments](https://dca.georgia.gov/document/document/ipc-2026-amendment-packet-2024-edition/download). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Floor area per person: 2024 International Building Code as adopted by Georgia, Table 1004.5, read on [UpCodes' copy of the Georgia Building Code 2024](https://up.codes/viewer/georgia/ibc-2024/chapter/10/means-of-egress). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Local amendments must be at least as strict as the state code: Georgia Department of Community Affairs, [Enforcement of State Minimum Codes](https://dca.georgia.gov/community-assistance/construction-codes/enforcement-state-minimum-codes) (O.C.G.A. 8-2-25). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Fire test for solid plastic partitions: 2024 International Building Code as adopted by Georgia, Sections 803.9 and 803.1.1 (NFPA 286) and the Section 202 definition of interior wall and ceiling finish, read on [UpCodes' copy of the Georgia Building Code 2024](https://up.codes/viewer/georgia/ibc-2024/chapter/8/interior-finishes); the Codes Reference Guide in the [state amendments](https://dca.georgia.gov/document/document/ibc-2026-amendment-packet-2024-edition/download) names the Life Safety Code (NFPA 101) as the primary code for interior finish, as do the [Rules of the Safety Fire Commissioner, Chapter 120-3-3](https://oci.georgia.gov/document/document/120-3-3/download). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Georgia access rules: [Rules of the Safety Fire Commissioner, Chapter 120-3-20, Access To and Use of Public Facilities by Handicapped Persons, effective January 1, 2015](https://ada.georgia.gov/document/publication/effective-january-1st-2015-access-and-use-public-facilities-handicapped/download), published on the [State ADA Coordinator's Office page](https://ada.georgia.gov/helpful-resources/advocacy-and-regulations/georgia-accessibility-code), and the [2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design](https://www.access-board.gov/ada/). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Single-user restroom signs: 2024 International Plumbing Code as adopted by Georgia, Section 403.1.2, read on [UpCodes' copy](https://up.codes/viewer/georgia/ipc-2024/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Restrooms in schools: [Senate Bill 1 (2025), the Riley Gaines Act, as signed](https://gov.georgia.gov/document/2025-signed-legislation/sb-1/download), amending O.C.G.A. 20-2-315. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wages on public jobs: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, [Dollar Threshold Amount for Contract Coverage Under State Prevailing Wage Laws](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/state/prevailing-wages), which lists Georgia among the states without a prevailing wage law. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax: Georgia Department of Revenue, [Sales and Use Tax Rate Chart effective October 1, 2026](https://dor.georgia.gov/document/document/httpsdorgeorgiagovdocumentdocumentgeneral-rate-chart-effective-october-1-2026/download) (state rate 4%), [What is Subject to Sales and Use Tax?](https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/sales-use-tax/what-subject-sales-and-use-tax) (freight taxable; itemized installation labor not taxable; use tax), [Policy Bulletin SUT-2019-02, Remote Sellers](https://dor.georgia.gov/document/document-sut-pb/sut-2019-02/download) and [Tax Guide for Contractors](https://dor.georgia.gov/tax-guide-contractors) with Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 560-12-2-.26, read on [Cornell LII](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/georgia/Ga-Comp-R-Regs-R-560-12-2-.26). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Georgia Accessibility Code (Rules of the Safety Fire Commissioner, Chapter 120-3-20, effective January 1, 2015); Georgia State Minimum Standard Building Code (2024 International Building Code with Georgia Amendments, effective January 1, 2026); Georgia State Minimum Standard Plumbing Code (2024 International Plumbing Code with Georgia Amendments, effective January 1, 2026); NFPA 286 for HDPE.

to_confirm: Toilet-count rows and Sections 403.1.1, 403.2, 424.2 were read on UpCodes, not on ICC's site (codes.iccsafe.org loads text by script). Georgia's own amendment PDF confirms the table rows are unchanged apart from service sinks and the residential row. Browser check on codes.iccsafe.org/content/IPC2024P1 before launch.

HDPE fire test: IBC 803.9 is in the adopted building code, but Georgia's Codes Reference Guide and Rule 120-3-3 put interior finish under the Life Safety Code (NFPA 101), whose text could not be read. Ask the State Fire Marshal's Office (404-656-2064) which text plan reviewers apply to toilet partitions, and which NFPA 101 edition is in force (the 120-3-3 PDF read shows the 2018 edition; a newer filing may exist, since rules.sos.ga.gov returned 403).

Occupant load: the Codes Reference Guide makes the Life Safety Code primary for means of egress. The IBC Table 1004.5 figures (150, 15, 20 square feet) were read; the Life Safety Code's table was not. Local plan review sets the number.

Whether a shared all-gender multi-user restroom may be built in addition to the required separate rooms, now that Georgia has deleted IPC 403.2 Exception 6 and 403.1.1 Exception 2: ask DCA Construction Codes (404-679-3118) or the Atlanta and Savannah building departments.
Atlanta and Savannah local amendments to the plumbing and building codes (allowed if stricter): city agent.

O.C.G.A. Title 30, Chapter 3 (the access statute) and O.C.G.A. 20-2-315 as codified were not read on the legislature's code site; SB 1 was read as the signed bill on the Governor's site. The bill text read has no effective date clause; a search result gave July 1, 2025, unverified.

Prevailing wage: the U.S. Department of Labor page is dated January 1, 2023 and was read through the fetch tool only. No Georgia statute was read. Whether Atlanta or Savannah put wage terms in their own construction contracts is for the city agent.

Sales tax on a furnish-and-install contract: Rule 560-12-2-.26 was read on Cornell LII (the Secretary of State's rules site returned 403), first paragraphs only. Confirm with the Department of Revenue (1-877-423-6711) how the owner is billed, and whether installed toilet partitions are treated as an improvement to real property.
Local sales tax rates change quarterly (chart read: effective October 1, 2026; Atlanta 8.9%, Chatham County 7%). How Next Partitions itself charges Georgia tax is a question for Abe's accountant.
